phase_name: Nested derivations of the CS5 axioms

objectives.description: Add the cut rule (eq. (3.1)) to NestedProof, InputCtx-shaped mirroring impL's output-pruning pattern, plus NestedProof.CutFree gating it out (mirroring SeqProof.cut/CutFree in LJ/Basic.lean)
Verify (in Lean) the exact shape of eq. (3.1)'s nec/w/cut rules against page 7 of the source, and Figure 5 (page 13) / Proposition 3.1 (page 7, general id) against direct PDF render
Prove Proposition 3.1 (general id: Gamma{A-bullet,A-circ} derivable for arbitrary formula A, not just atomic) as reusable machinery for all 17 axiom derivations
objectives.blocker: See handoffs/phase-14-handoff-20260726.md. Rigorously verified (two Lean lemmas, buildRhsChain_box_shape / InputCtx_fillLhs_snd_box / InputCtx_fillEmpty_snd_box) that every InputCtx-shaped NestedProof constructor (botL, w if added, cut, contract, andL, boxL, diaL, tL, fourL, bStruct) produces a conclusion whose RHS component is unconditionally `.box`-shaped, never `.atom`-shaped -- regardless of context length. The bare, top-level target needed by impR's premise (and hence by every axiom whose Hilbert schema is an implication, which is all 17) requires an `.atom`-shaped RHS at context length 0 or 1. The only rule producing `.atom`-shaped RHS at that length is `id`, restricted to a base-type Atom on both sides (not usable when a schema variable is instantiated at `Proposition.bot` or any compound formula). This blocks the A = bot base case of general id in particular, hence efq directly, and -- because implyK/andE1/etc. are universally quantified over arbitrary formulas that could syntactically be `Proposition.bot` -- transitively blocks every other axiom depending on general id.
